title: Cuman-Kipchak Confederation
capsule: The Cuman-Kipchak Confederation was a loose alliance of Turkic nomadic peoples — the Cumans west of the Volga and the Kipchaks east of it — who dominated the western Eurasian steppe (Dasht-i Qipchaq) from roughly the mid-11th century. At their height in the 12th century they controlled territory from the Danube to the Irtish, raided the Rus' principalities and the Byzantine Empire, and formed matrimonial alliances with the rulers of Hungary and Georgia. The confederation was shattered by the Mongol campaigns of 1237–1241 under Batu Khan and Subutai; its survivors fled into Hungary, Bulgaria, and the Sultanate of Rum, where they left a lasting demographic imprint.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is broadly attested through medieval chronicles and archaeological evidence but the confederation lacked fixed borders; maps represent a general zone of dominance rather than administered territory.
